body:
There are two issues here:
1. When the PHP intl extension is not installed Symfony's stub implementation is used instead, and its `StubNumberFormatter::getErrorCode()` always returns U_ZERO_ERROR. Since this is not a failure code, an exception will not be raised and the false value returned by `StubNumberFormatter::parse()` for invalid arguments will be used as the transformed value. Obviously, this boolean is not a valid number, so when it is checked elsewhere, the UnexpectedTypeException will be raised.
2. The integer-string transformer is indiscriminately casting anything it is given to an integer, rather than letting the number formatter handle type casting. This results in invalid values becoming valid integers and therefore not triggering any exceptions.

I am working on patches for these issues.

issue.title: Let NumberFormatter handle integer type casting
issue.body:
The integer to localised string transformer is currently casting everything it gets to an integer, even if it is not a number. This responsibility should be passed off to NumberFormatter.

Partially addresses #2389 by not mistakenly typecasting a boolean false into an integer 0

issue.title: Set error code when number cannot be parsed in StubNumberFormatter
issue.body:
The stub implementation of NumberFormatter never sets an error code and instead always returns the "no-error" code. This causes unexpected results when a transformer gives it bad arguments, such as transforming the input value to boolean false and causing exceptions further down the line, as in #2389.

Instead, it should set an error code when appropriate and return it when requested so that a TransformationFailedException can be raised and the input value left unaltered.

There may be other instances where an error should be set. This covers the common use case of non-numeric input.

Bug fix: yes
Feature addition: no
Backwards compatibility break: no
Symfony2 tests pass: yes
Fixes the following tickets: #2389

Ran into the same problem on Symfony 2.7.6. If you use form field type "integer", non-numeric inputs such as "asdf" will not be handled correctly. A workaround is to use an integer DB column, the form field type "text" and a Regex constraint with the pattern /^[1-9][0-9]*$/
